unsupported_codes.reason: Poisoning by, adverse effect of and underdosing of systemic antibiotics, the category that holds the fluoroquinolone codes: reporting a code from it states that the antibiotic caused a drug event such as the tendinitis, and the provider states no cause.
Poisoning by, adverse effect of and underdosing of other systemic anti-infectives and antiparasitics: the same assumption, under another drug category.

citations.M76.62: ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY2027, Section I.A.19: the assignment of a diagnosis code is based on the provider's diagnostic statement that the condition exists. Section I.A.15: for conditions not specifically linked by relational terms in the classification, provider documentation must link the conditions in order to code them as related. Section I.C.19.e.5.a: an adverse effect of a drug that was correctly prescribed and properly administered is reported with a code for the nature of the adverse effect, followed by the code for the adverse effect of the drug. Here the surgeon's diagnosis is Achilles tendinitis of the left leg; the note records a finished course of levofloxacin in the history, states no cause for the tendinitis and does not link it to the antibiotic, so no adverse effect is documented and the tendinitis is reported alone.

coder_notes: The timing makes a link to the antibiotic clinically likely, but the link is the provider's to make. The ankle pain and swelling are part of the tendinitis. Examination and ultrasound show no tear, so no rupture code applies. The antibiotic course was ten days and had ended, so no long-term drug therapy code is reported. In practice this documentation would lead to a provider query; the gold is what can be reported from the note as written.
